query: Bug report: st.button returns False on the rerun after a click. I already logged both return values. Is this expected? Streamlit version unknown.

candidates.title: button-behavior-and-examples
candidates.section: Summary
candidates.text:
## Summary

Buttons created with [`st.button`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.button) do not retain state. They return `True` on the script rerun resulting from their click and immediately return to `False` on the next script rerun. If a displayed element is nested inside `if st.button('Click me'):`, the element will be visible when the button is clicked and disappear as soon as the user takes their next action. This is because the script reruns and the button return value becomes `False`.

In this guide, we will illustrate the use of buttons and explain common misconceptions. Read on to see a variety of examples that expand on `st.button` using [`st.session_state`](/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.session_state). [Anti-patterns](#anti-patterns) are included at the end. Go ahead and pull up your favorite code editor so you can `streamlit run` the examples as you read. Check out Streamlit's [Basic concepts](/get-started/fundamentals/main-concepts) if you haven't run your own Streamlit scripts yet.

I'm getting the same behaviour with the nightly build. I played around and found that it also happens outside a fragment:

```
import streamlit as st

if st.button("rerun"):
    st.rerun()
t = st.text_input("Enter t:",value='foo')
st.info(f't = {t}')
```

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

Ah, so it's a similar problem. The rerun is abandoning the text input before it's rendered and therefore loses its value.

I do think there's something to be said that the return value of text input should be what the user sees inside. This makes sense from a developer experience.

That being said, the recommended way to make this work would be to run `st.rerun` after the text input to maintain the top down script paradigm.

```python
import streamlit as st

bar =st.empty()
t = st.text_input("Enter t:",value='foo')
if bar.button("rerun"):
    st.rerun()
st.info(f't = {t}')
```

Okay, I guess you can close this. Thanks for your help.

btw, I think https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/3533 describes the issue clearly. We'll have to investigate some more.

candidates.section: Additional Information
candidates.text:
### Additional Information

_No response_

Hey [USER] Thank you for the issue! I believe this is an expected behavior. Widgets that don't appear in the run are deleted. Here's what's happening:

1. Text is updated in string
2. Button is pressed and rerun occurs (but the the text was never rendered. Widget is reset
3. Widget reverts back to default

If you move the rerun button _after_ the text input. Everything works as expected. If you want it before the text input, you can leverage `st.empty()` like in this example:

```python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment()
def toggle_and_text():
    foo = st.empty()
    t = st.text_input("Enter t:",value='foo', key='t')
    st.info(f't = {t}')
    if foo.button("rerun"):
        st.rerun()

toggle_and_text()
st.header('Outside Fragment')
st.info(f'session_state_t = {st.session_state.t}')
st.button("Update")
```

I'll probably close this issue, but feel free to ask any questions

Okay, this makes sense. But, in that case, shouldn't the value in the text_input also be updated to the default when you click "rerun".

candidates.title: button-behavior-and-examples
candidates.section: A slight problem
candidates.text:
#### A slight problem

In this example, we access `st.session_state.name` both before and after the buttons which modify it. When a button ("**Jane**" or "**John**") is clicked, the script reruns. The info displayed before the buttons lags behind the info written after the button. The data in `st.session_state` before the button is not updated. When the script executes the button function, that is when the conditional code to update `st.session_state` creates the change. Thus, this change is reflected after the button.

```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

if 'name' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['name'] = 'John Doe'

st.header(st.session_state['name'])

if st.button('Jane'):
    st.session_state['name'] = 'Jane Doe'

if st.button('John'):
    st.session_state['name'] = 'John Doe'

st.header(st.session_state['name'])
```

candidates.title: Multiselect Visual State vs Returned Value Mismatch
candidates.section: Additional Information
candidates.text:
There is a workaround for this by using a placeholder and checking the button click at the end of the script (or saving the click value and running rerun at the end of the rerun), e.g.:

````python
# Sidebar with reload button (matching original pattern)
with st.sidebar:
    st.header("Data Management")
    reloade_button_container = st.container()

# Rest of the app....

with reloade_button_container:
    if st.button("🔄 Reload Data", help="Clear cache and reload"):
        load_test_data.clear()
        st.success("Cache cleared! Data will be reloaded.")
        st.rerun()
````

Closing this issue since we have a feature request to provide a way to keep the widget state even when a widget isn't rendered for a rerun: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6074 Feel free to upvote and engage on this feature request.

candidates.section: Reproducible Code Example
candidates.text:
### Reproducible Code Example

[[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-12305)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# Cached data function that returns test data
@st.cache_data
def load_test_data():
    return pd.DataFrame({
        'id': ['item_1', 'item_2', 'item_3'],
        'type': ['TypeA', 'TypeB', 'TypeC'],
        'value': [100, 200, 300]
    })

st.title("Multiselect Bug Reproducer")

# Sidebar with reload button (matching original pattern)
with st.sidebar:
    st.header("Data Management")
    if st.button("🔄 Reload Data", help="Clear cache and reload"):
        load_test_data.clear()
        st.success("Cache cleared! Data will be reloaded.")
        st.rerun()

# Load data
df = load_test_data()

# Extract unique types (matching original pattern)
all_types = sorted(df['type'].dropna().unique())

# Sidebar filters (matching original pattern)
st.sidebar.header("Filters") 

# Create multiselect in sidebar with all types as default
selected_types = st.sidebar.multiselect(
    "Select Types",
    all_types,
    default=all_types,  # All selected by default
)

# Filter data based on selection
filtered_df = df.copy()
if selected_types:
    filtered_df = filtered_df[filtered_df['type'].isin(selected_types)]

# Show debug info that reveals the bug
st.write("### Debug Information:")
st.write(f"**Multiselect shows selected**: {selected_types}")
st.write(f"**Filtered data rows**: {len(filtered_df)}")
st.write(f"**Item IDs in filtered data**: {sorted(filtered_df['id'].tolist())}")

st.write("---")
st.write("### Steps to reproduce bug:")
st.write("1. Initially all types are selected → shows 3 rows")
st.write("2. **In sidebar, deselect 'TypeA'** → should show 2 rows")
st.write("3. **Click 'Reload Data' button in sidebar**")
st.write("4. **BUG**: Sidebar shows 'TypeB, TypeC' but filtered data includes all 3 rows")

st.write("### Show actual data:")
st.dataframe(filtered_df)
```

I originally discussed this [here]( https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/clearing-cache-on-a-single-method-screws-up-multiselect-selected-items/119093) and it looks like [this discussion](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/multipage-with-multiselect-default-and-session-state/52619) may also be relevant. 

  Related GitHub Issues:
  - Issue #6079: "session_state not actually changed until second page reload" - Documents that session_state doesn't update immediately after widget interaction, requiring double reloads
  - Issue #4223: "Issue in multiselect - default and current value overlap" - Reports similar problems where default parameters conflict with current selections in multiselect widgets
  - Issue #4695: "multiselect reset to defaults behavior is inconsistent" - Documents inconsistent behavior when multiselect widgets reset to defaults during reruns

[USER] Thanks for reporting this issue. I reproduced it [here](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-12305). The behaviour you are seeing is annoying but currently expected. This is caused by the `st.rerun()` being used in the middle of the script -> which causes the following widgets not being rendered for one rerun -> which causes the widget state to be cleaned up. 

There is a workaround for this by using a placeholder and checking the button click at the end of the script (or saving the click value and running rerun at the end of the rerun), e.g.:

````python
# Sidebar with reload button (matching original pattern)
with st.sidebar:
    st.header("Data Management")
    reloade_button_container = st.container()

# Rest of the app....

with reloade_button_container:
    if st.button("🔄 Reload Data", help="Clear cache and reload"):
        load_test_data.clear()
        st.success("Cache cleared! Data will be reloaded.")
        st.rerun()
````

Closing this issue since we have a feature request to provide a way to keep the widget state even when a widget isn't rendered for a rerun: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6074 Feel free to upvote and engage on this feature request.

candidates.title: download_button with data=callable runs without ScriptRunContext
candidates.text:
### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.52.2
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: Win
- Browser: Chrome

Somehow I missed this issue https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13337
Closing as duplicate

Confirming this from a production incident — and it's a bit worse than "missing ScriptRunContext produces a warning": inside that thread, `st.session_state` reads return stale values and `@st.cache_data`-wrapped calls silently return whatever was already cached, **with no error and no warning**. Both just look like they worked.

Our incident: a `data=callable` on `st.download_button` called into functions that (transitively) read `@st.cache_data`-cached helpers. Because those calls run outside `ScriptRunContext`, they picked up cached results from a *different* request context — users occasionally downloaded a file that didn't match what they'd just generated on screen, with nothing in the logs to explain why. ## Summary

Buttons created with [`st.button`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.button) do not retain state. They return `True` on the script rerun resulting from their click and immediately return to `False` on the next script rerun. If a displayed element is nested inside `if st.button('Click me'):`, the element will be visible when the button is clicked and disappear as soon as the user takes their next action. This is because the script reruns and the button return value becomes `False`.

In this guide, we will illustrate the use of buttons and explain common misconceptions. Read on to see a variety of examples that expand on `st.button` using [`st.session_state`](/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.session_state). There is a workaround for this by using a placeholder and checking the button click at the end of the script (or saving the click value and running rerun at the end of the rerun), e.g.:

with reloade_button_container:

        st.success("Cache cleared! Data will be reloaded.")
        st.rerun()

parent.text:
### Additional Information

I originally discussed this [here]( https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/clearing-cache-on-a-single-method-screws-up-multiselect-selected-items/119093) and it looks like [this discussion](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/multipage-with-multiselect-default-and-session-state/52619) may also be relevant. 

  Related GitHub Issues:
  - Issue #6079: "session_state not actually changed until second page reload" - Documents that session_state doesn't update immediately after widget interaction, requiring double reloads
  - Issue #4223: "Issue in multiselect - default and current value overlap" - Reports similar problems where default parameters conflict with current selections in multiselect widgets
  - Issue #4695: "multiselect reset to defaults behavior is inconsistent" - Documents inconsistent behavior when multiselect widgets reset to defaults during reruns

[USER] Thanks for reporting this issue. I reproduced it [here](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-12305). The behaviour you are seeing is annoying but currently expected. This is caused by the `st.rerun()` being used in the middle of the script -> which causes the following widgets not being rendered for one rerun -> which causes the widget state to be cleaned up. 

There is a workaround for this by using a placeholder and checking the button click at the end of the script (or saving the click value and running rerun at the end of the rerun), e.g.:

````python
# Sidebar with reload button (matching original pattern)
with st.sidebar:
    st.header("Data Management")
    reloade_button_container = st.container()

# Rest of the app....

with reloade_button_container:
    if st.button("🔄 Reload Data", help="Clear cache and reload"):
        load_test_data.clear()
        st.success("Cache cleared! Data will be reloaded.")
        st.rerun()
````

Closing this issue since we have a feature request to provide a way to keep the widget state even when a widget isn't rendered for a rerun: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6074 Feel free to upvote and engage on this feature request.

## Summary

Buttons created with [`st.button`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.button) do not retain state. They return `True` on the script rerun resulting from their click and immediately return to `False` on the next script rerun. If a displayed element is nested inside `if st.button('Click me'):`, the element will be visible when the button is clicked and disappear as soon as the user takes their next action. This is because the script reruns and the button return value becomes `False`.

In this guide, we will illustrate the use of buttons and explain common misconceptions. Read on to see a variety of examples that expand on `st.button` using [`st.session_state`](/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.session_state). ### Additional Information

_No response_

Hey [USER] Thank you for the issue! I believe this is an expected behavior. Widgets that don't appear in the run are deleted. Here's what's happening:

1. Text is updated in string
2. Button is pressed and rerun occurs (but the the text was never rendered. Widget is reset
3. Widget reverts back to default

If you move the rerun button _after_ the text input. Everything works as expected. If you want it before the text input, you can leverage `st.empty()` like in this example:

```python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment()
def toggle_and_text():
    foo = st.empty()
    t = st.text_input("Enter t:",value='foo', key='t')
    st.info(f't = {t}')
    if foo.button("rerun"):
        st.rerun()

toggle_and_text()
st.header('Outside Fragment')
st.info(f'session_state_t = {st.session_state.t}')
st.button("Update")
```

I'll probably close this issue, but feel free to ask any questions

Okay, this makes sense. But, in that case, shouldn't the value in the text_input also be updated to the default when you click "rerun".

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

Hmmm it updates for me. Are you clicking the button while the text input still has focus? I wonder if there's a race condition happening

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

What you see is what I get after clicking "Update", not "rerun". When I click "rerun", I get the inconsistency.  It behaves the same whether or not the text input is in focus.

I get both values still. Can you try with the latest nightly? `pip install streamlit-nightly` might need to uninstall Streamlit.

I'm getting the same behaviour with the nightly build. I played around and found that it also happens outside a fragment:

```
import streamlit as st

if st.button("rerun"):
    st.rerun()
t = st.text_input("Enter t:",value='foo')
st.info(f't = {t}')
```

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

Ah, so it's a similar problem. The rerun is abandoning the text input before it's rendered and therefore loses its value.

I do think there's something to be said that the return value of text input should be what the user sees inside. This makes sense from a developer experience.

That being said, the recommended way to make this work would be to run `st.rerun` after the text input to maintain the top down script paradigm.

```python
import streamlit as st

bar =st.empty()
t = st.text_input("Enter t:",value='foo')
if bar.button("rerun"):
    st.rerun()
st.info(f't = {t}')
```

Okay, I guess you can close this. Thanks for your help.

btw, I think https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/3533 describes the issue clearly. We'll have to investigate some more.
